claims.text: Helm is a graduated Cloud Native Computing Foundation project.
Helm is open source under Apache License 2.0 and the Helm project does not ship a commercial tier.
In Pulumi, resource ordering is derived from the dependency graph: each resource waits for its dependencies to become ready, and independent resources deploy in parallel.
Helm installs resources in a fixed order by Kubernetes kind, defined in pkg/release/v1/util/kind_sorter.go in the Helm source.
Helm chart authors cannot declare dependencies between resources or subcharts, except through hook weights.
The Helm docs state: "the Kubernetes objects from the charts and all its dependencies are aggregated into a single set; then sorted by type followed by name; and then created/updated in that order."

Helm's kind sort order begins with PriorityClasses and Namespaces, then Secrets and ConfigMaps, then CustomResourceDefinitions and RBAC, then Services and workloads, with unlisted kinds (including custom resources) last.
Helm uninstall runs the kind ordering list in reverse.
Helm sends sorted manifests to the API server in a single pass and doesn't wait for one resource to become ready before applying the next.
Helm chart dependencies (subcharts) have their objects merged into the parent chart's set and sorted by kind, so a chart cannot express installing one subchart before another.
Helm chart hooks ordered by helm.sh/hook-weight annotations are a workaround for ordering, and hook resources are not managed by Helm as part of the release.
Native sequencing for resources and subcharts has been proposed in HIP-0025, which is still a draft.
In Pulumi, passing one resource's output to another or setting the dependsOn resource option creates an edge in the dependency graph.
The Pulumi Kubernetes provider waits for each resource to become ready before creating dependents and deploys independent resources in parallel.
Pulumi deletes follow the dependency graph in reverse.
Pulumi's helm.v4.Chart supports the config.kubernetes.io/depends-on annotation for ordering between objects inside the chart, and dependsOn on the chart for dependencies on outside resources.
Pulumi's dependency-ordered parallel deployment makes updates faster than a strict serial sequence.
Helm SDK is available in Go only; other languages must shell out to the helm CLI.
Pulumi Policies is open source, with rules in Python, TypeScript, or OPA Rego; the Enterprise edition adds Pulumi-maintained policy packs for CIS, PCI DSS, HITRUST, and NIST.
A failed Pulumi update leaves the stack partially updated, and you roll forward by reverting program code and running pulumi up.
Two patterns cover most production deployments of using Pulumi and Helm together.
Pulumi resolves chart values at deploy time and orders the chart install after its dependencies.
Using Helm charts directly from a Pulumi program is the most common adoption pattern for adopting Pulumi alongside Helm.
helm.v4.Chart registers each rendered Kubernetes object as a Pulumi resource, so every child shows up in plan output, drift detection, and state.
Helm merges objects from a chart and its dependencies into a single set, sorts them by kind, and applies them in that order, so declaring a subchart as a dependency doesn't make it install first.
Pulumi creates and deletes resources in dependency order, with each resource ready before dependents.
